summary: The remainder operator casts its operands to integers and computes the remainder after division.
documentation: The remainder operator casts its operands to integers and computes the remainder after division. A divisor of zero produces NULL. Negative dividends can produce negative remainders; remainder is not the same as a nonnegative modulo operation.
returns: id and slot, ordered by id.
caution: For portable nonnegative slots across signed input, normalize the remainder with a second remainder operation. This exercise uses a fixed positive divisor.
scenarios: Assign imported batch numbers to four rotating review queues.
Distribute signed sequence identifiers across local buckets.
Cycle a repeating four-position display from integer counters.
title: Normalize four queue slots
problem: For every job, return id and ((batch_no % 4) + 4) % 4 AS slot, ordered by id. Negative batch numbers must still produce slots 0..3; NULL stays NULL.
goal: Use Remainder operator (%) or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: The extra addition and remainder normalize a negative remainder.
